question: Does the locatable_sample's fixed per-page-type template composition explain the parent's zero task-type discrimination (eta-squared=0.0), and does the full DOM contain task-type-discriminative tag structure that the sample masks?
hypothesis: The 20-element locatable_sample is a fixed template per page type: all tasks of the same page type share identical element tags, roles, inForm flags, and bbox coordinates. This makes eta-squared=0.0 a mathematical necessity for ANY density recipe, because there is zero within-page-type variance in the sample. The full DOM, by contrast, exhibits genuine task-type variation in tag distribution, DOM size, and element counts (e.g., listing DOMs have ~1700 elements with ~400 links, detail DOMs have ~1300 elements with ~330 links, cart DOMs have ~1136 elements with ~320 links).
falsifier: The template-composition explanation is falsified if ANY of: (F1) Within at least one page type, the locatable_sample elements differ across tasks in tag, role, inForm, or bbox (i.e., the sample is NOT a fixed template); (F2) A metric computed from the locatable_sample (e.g., tag entropy, form fraction, element count) achieves eta-squared >= 0.10 on page_type, showing the sample contains task-type-discriminative information; (F3) The full DOM tag distribution does NOT differ significantly across page types (chi-squared p > 0.05), meaning the full DOM also lacks task-type structure.

baselines.description: Parent hierarchy-weighted density eta-squared = 0.0 on page_type (EXP-INTEL-35401997918 M7). All density recipes (canonical, weighted, hierarchy) produce identical within-type means.
Parent Spearman(hierarchy, weighted) = 1.0 at alpha=0.3 (EXP-INTEL-35401997918 M6). The hierarchy recipe is a monotonic reparameterization of weighted, confirming zero structural novelty.
Full DOM tag counts vary across tasks: listing div=163-171, a=399-403; detail div=98-126, a=328-329; cart div=43, a=320. This variation is absent from the locatable_sample.

positive_control.description: The full DOM tag distribution differs significantly across page types (listing/detail/cart). Chi-squared test on tag-type counts should yield p < 0.01.
positive_control.expected: Full DOM chi-squared p < 0.01, confirming the full DOM has task-type structure that the locatable_sample masks.

null_control.description: The locatable_sample tag composition is identical across all tasks within each page type. Any metric computed from the sample (tag entropy, form fraction, element count) should have zero within-type variance.
null_control.expected: Within-type standard deviation of sample metrics = 0.0 for all tested metrics, confirming the template invariance.

measurement_validity: All computations use existing raw evidence from EXP-INTEL-34782350557 (sha256: da30bd059adb555409784a2fd41402d53b64a25c89aa710b77e686a94a155050). No new data collection required.
The locatable_sample elements are compared field-by-field (tag, role, inForm, x, y, w, h) to verify template identity.
Full DOM tag distributions are extracted from dom_stats.tagCounts for each task.
Tag-type chi-squared test uses the full DOM counts aggregated by page type.
Metrics are bounded to 7 tasks (3 listing, 3 detail, 1 cart*2), 1 Magento site, 3 definitions. No cross-site extrapolation.
*cart_1 appears twice in the raw data (duplicate entry); treated as single task.
decision_rule:
Conjunctive:

C1_SAMPLE_TEMPLATE_INVARIANT: For each page type, the locatable_sample elements are identical across all tasks of that type (all fields: tag, role, inForm, x, y, w, h). PASS if 100% identical within each type; FAIL if any within-type difference exists.

C2_SAMPLE_ETA2_ZERO: The eta-squared of ANY sample-derived metric (tag entropy, form fraction, total_area) on page_type is < 0.01 (effectively zero). PASS if all tested metrics have eta2 < 0.01; FAIL if any metric achieves eta2 >= 0.01.

C3_FULL_DOM_DISCRIMINATES: The full DOM tag-type distribution differs significantly across page types (chi-squared p < 0.01). PASS if p < 0.01; FAIL if p >= 0.01.

C4_INFORMATION_LOSS: The mutual information between tag composition and page_type is 0.0 for the locatable_sample and > 0.0 for the full DOM. PASS if I_sample = 0.0 AND I_full_dom > 0.0; FAIL otherwise.

VERDICT RULES:
- If C1 AND C2 AND C3 AND C4: CONFIRMS — template composition explains zero eta-squared. Full DOM has task-type structure. MIXED program viable if per-task sampling obtained.
- If NOT C1: FALSIFIES template explanation — sample IS per-task, and density failure is genuine. MIXED program should be abandoned for this sample.
- If C1 AND C2 AND NOT C3: MIXED program limited by page structure, not sample. Full DOM also lacks task-type variation. Abandon density-based MIXED.
- If C1 AND NOT C2: Sample has task-type structure (unexpected). Density recipes may work with richer sample metrics.
- If NOT C3: Full DOM also lacks task-type structure. The MIXED program is limited by the Magento site's page-type homogeneity, not by the sampling procedure.
product_consequence_positive: The MIXED program's failure is attributed to sampling procedure (fixed template), not density metric limitation. Product lane can pursue MIXED resolution by obtaining per-task locatable_samples from the runtime lane. The 31x canonical/weighted material gap (EXP-INTEL-35264637598) remains usable if per-task samples are available.
product_consequence_negative: If the full DOM also lacks task-type structure (C3 fails), the MIXED program is limited by the Magento site's page-type homogeneity. Density-based MIXED handling should be abandoned for this site, and the lane should pivot to cross-site testing or alternative metrics.
estimated_cost: VERY LOW — offline computation on existing reconstructed data. No browser/network work. Field-by-field comparison of 20-element samples (7 tasks x 20 elements x 7 fields = 980 comparisons). Tag-count chi-squared (3 page types x ~15 tag categories). Mutual information estimation. Estimated < 1000 LLM tokens.
expected_information_gain: HIGH — directly diagnoses WHY the parent experiment produced eta-squared=0.0. If the template explanation is confirmed, the MIXED program has a clear path forward (per-task sampling). If falsified, the MIXED program should be abandoned or redirected. Either outcome resolves the parent's open question U-1 and prevents wasted cycles on density recipes applied to template samples.
